column1: # JITLua-5.4 differential harness: known DIFFERENCES from PUC-Lua 5.4.9.
# Not defects: deliberate fork decisions (FORK), behaviour the 5.4 manual leaves
# to the implementation (IMPL-DEFINED), or inherited LuaJIT extensions. Each one
# is also described in docs/DIFFERENCES.md. Real defects are in known-bad.tsv.

column3: FORK: the __call chain (lines 171/193) is fixed; the only remaining mode-A difference is the binary-chunk section, which compares our private `\27LJ...` dump header to PUC's `\27Lua...` (line 474). Mode R checks our own dump format.

IMPL-DEFINED: under a 4GiB RLIMIT_AS (--include-heavy) both sides end in an allowed resource error but cannot match: measured on x86_64 and aarch64, PUC reports "not enough memory" at #a=134217728 (peak ~2.0GiB RSS; the stop size varies with allocator fragmentation) while LuaJIT also reports "not enough memory", at #a=268435456 (collectgarbage'count' ~2.15GiB); with a 14GiB cap PUC stops at #a=536870912 and LuaJIT at #a=1073741824 (~8.59GiB counted); the per-MiB stderr counters differ in every mode.
IMPL-DEFINED: dump/reload border bug FIXED and rawlen added; only the runtime-built sparse-table border differs (any border is legal per the 5.4 manual)
IMPL-DEFINED: runtime-built sparse tables may report any legal border (5.4 manual 3.4.7); LuaJIT's array-growth policy differs from PUC's alimit hint
FORK: private dump format (JITLua-5.4 fork); PUC 5.4.9 cannot round-trip it, mode R checks ours

KNOWN DIVERGENCE (inherited): the backported LuaJIT v3.0 "Short Function Expression" (doc/extensions.html) accepts `a->b` / `|x|->...`; PUC 5.4.9 rejects it. Downstream lume 2.3.0 relies on the rejection (docs/notes/downstream-2026-11.md). EXTENSION in docs/DIFFERENCES.md.

IMPL-DEFINED + FORK: runs like PUC up to the finalizer test (line 913), which loops until a table that is only referenced from a dead argument slot of the main chunk is finalized; the stack is scanned conservatively up to the frame top (inherited from LuaJIT, the manual does not say when an object becomes garbage), so the loop does not end and every arm runs into the runner's 10 s bound for this file (tests/lib/runner.py). With that loop bypassed the only other difference is the stripped chunk at line 1002: the private dump format drops linedefined when stripping (PUC keeps it). See docs/notes/istailcall.md.

IMPL-DEFINED: stack-overflow depth differs (PUC grows to LUAI_MAXSTACK=1e6 slots, this tree stops at LJ_STACK_MAX+LJ_STACK_ERREX): the suite prints "final count: 250043" (x86_64) / 250044 (arm64) for PUC vs 13100 here. The line-29 assertion is fixed (tests/d54/err_11_errerr_msg.lua); see docs/DIFFERENCES.md
IMPL-DEFINED: the overflow depth differs by a frame between the JIT on/off arms (printed "final count" 13100 vs 13102, both architectures); see docs/DIFFERENCES.md
IMPL-DEFINED: the overflow depth differs by the frames of the dump/reload wrapper (printed "final count" 13100 direct vs 13103 reloaded, both architectures); see docs/DIFFERENCES.md

IMPL-DEFINED + FORK: the last block (assert at line 122) counts basic GC steps -- it expects one collectgarbage("step", 0) to clear an old weak table's young value. A basic step here does GCSTEPSIZE/100*stepmul bytes of collector work (~2 KB, src/lj_gc.c), PUC's basic step far more: the entry dies after 1 step in PUC, in incremental and in generational mode alike, and after 12 steps here; with collectgarbage("setstepmul", 20000) ours also clears it in one step and reports the finished cycle, so weak-table clearing itself matches. The file's generational section is inert on both sides: collectgarbage("generational") only records the mode flag (src/lj_api.c, "LuaJIT keeps one incremental GC"); the collector is the inherited incremental one (docs/gc-newgen-plan.md Stage 3, docs/plan.md P4.1 open). Measured the same on x86_64 and aarch64, -joff and -jon alike; repro tests/lib/gc-step-quantum-repro.lua. Entry "GC mode and the size of a basic step" in docs/DIFFERENCES.md.

IMPL-DEFINED + FORK: bounded at 10 s by the runner because GC1/GC2 (lines 63/82/87/92) wait for a finalizer of a table that a dead stack slot keeps alive here (PUC ends those loops after 39 iterations); the dead-slot entry in docs/DIFFERENCES.md, repro tests/lib/gc-finloop-repro.lua. Everything after line 339 is not reached, so the later weak-table lines are covered by repros, not by this run: line 323 (weak value still present inside the finalizer, PUC clears it in the atomic phase; tests/lib/gc-weak-finalizer-repro.lua), line 347 (ephemeron entries survive a full collection, PUC uses converged ephemeron marking; tests/lib/gc-ephemeron-repro.lua) and lines 475/487 (collectgarbage"count" after clearing a weak kv table: the 2^22-byte key stays interned here, FORK string interning, and count reports LuaJIT's allocation grain; measured 12288 vs 8192 KB after fill, 2045 vs 0.24 KB final on x86_64 and aarch64; tests/lib/gc-count-weak-repro.lua). All three are documented in docs/DIFFERENCES.md.

FORK: %p of two equal 300-byte strings (line 194) is the same address here because every string is interned, while PUC does not intern long strings (docs/DIFFERENCES.md, string-interning row; repro tests/lib/str-intern-ptr-repro.lua). Modes B and R compare our arms only and agree.

IMPL-DEFINED: tracegc.lua writes one "." to stderr per finished collection cycle; how many cycles the run triggers follows the collector's pacing (PUC printed 2 dots, this tree a different number, measured on x86_64 and arm64), stdout and the modes B and R match; see docs/DIFFERENCES.md (collection cycles)
